_doc: RimFlow v3.0 Dispatcher schedule (design/RimMandrake/rimflow_v3_2026-10-26.md §3: one schedule file runs every role). Read by src/RimMandrake/rimflow/dispatcher.py. Times in seconds. The owner sets this file; an enabled role with launch keys (instructions, seat, clone, model, ledger_item) is run by role_launch.py; the owner switched every role on 2026-10-28 (Conductor and Operations: Dispatcher wave 1, e35afe1dcc; Arbiter advisory, Producer, Auditor, Innovator: the v3 trial night, 4d9171a1e5). Token caps are admission checks at launch plus after-the-fact overbudget alarms, never a stop mid-run; only run_max_s stops a run (role_launch.py). Every role's throttle_bands are still computed and journaled, but every band runs like GREEN (slots all, quick_cap_x 1.0) since d92c4c825e, owner 2026-10-28: "Stop the whole account rated RED on runeway crap. Just do the checkout."; restoring a band is the owner's. throttle_order is read by no live program (only Utils/sim/rimflow_v3_sim.py).

no_handoff._doc: FOUNDRY_IDLE_REWIRE_PARKS_ON_LANE_WAITS (BENCH 2026-10-29): after a woke_no_handoff (doorbell consumed, no lease/claim/start in handoff_s) the seat is rung again after rering_s[k-1] s for its k-th consecutive one (the last entry bounds it), instead of the whole cooldown_s: that cooldown made ring FOUNDRY-1793297947-1 -> FOUNDRY-1793302231-1 4284 s apart (handoff_s 600 + cooldown_s 3600 + tick) while 798 items waited. Each ring is sent only when the seat's queue has work, so escalate_after consecutive ones raise an idle_full_queue:<SEAT> alarm (ledger note on escalate_item, null = alarm_item, rate-limited by alarm_every_s) and append a RAISE FIRST line to conductor_log (null = off). A hand-off or an empty queue ends the streak. Worst case: rings at ~0, ~16, ~43 min, then every ~40 min (handoff_s + 1800 + tick), escalated at ~53 min; under the 12/h cap.

long_helper._doc: CONDUCTOR_HELPERS_TUNE_TWENTY_MINUTE_WINDOW (owner 2026-10-29: "Long standing runs beyond n hour should raise an alarm in conductor."): a Conductor-window helper running longer than alarm_after_s raises a long_helper:<id> alarm (ledger note on item, null = alarm_item; RAISE FIRST line in no_handoff.conductor_log).

helper_budget._doc: HELPER_BUDGET_MIGRATE_INTO_DISPATCHER: every tick the Dispatcher publishes the helper budget (helper_budget.py -> <state>/helper_budget.json, seats CONDUCTOR/FOUNDRY) that the spawn hook reads first. false = the hook falls back to allocation.json/compute.

_token_notes_item_doc: review U N2: a dispatcher note holding a token term (ops_watch_rules.json token_talk.terms) bound for an item a token-blind role reads (any role ledger_item but a token_aware role's) goes here instead; Operations has its own ledger_item so its launch, done and cap notes never reach the shared table. The Producer still reads Operations' REPLAN REQUEST notes on its own ledger_item (operations.md: plan terms only, no numbers).

caps._why: BENCH 2026-10-29 (FOUNDRY_IDLE_DIAGNOSE_CAP_STARVES_TRIAGE): was 6/h, 48/day, 80 overall. After the v3 cutover FOUNDRY clears most rung tickets in under a minute (block/reconcile of old BENCH items), so 6 rings were spent by 04:35Z and the hour cap left the window at a bare prompt ~35 min/h (journal 04:10-04:35Z). A ring every ~4 min is the tick ceiling, ~15/h.

BENCH._names_why: CONDUCTOR_RCNAME_RENAME_DISPATCHER_ALIAS (owner 2026-10-29: 'So it's called bench again instead of conductor.'): the window is launched and SHOWN as CONDUCTOR (session --name, --remote-control, title hook); a window launched before the rename keeps 'AGENT BENCH' until its next relaunch, so every matcher takes both (session_match.names_of). Never 'AGENT CONDUCTOR': that is the Conductor role's window_name hold, and the hold must not fire on this tile (selftest_conductor_identity). Ledger key stays BENCH.
BENCH._why: BENCH is the owner's workshop window (the Conductor's session mode): watched, never woken or resumed by a program

golive._doc: The set the owner's switch may turn on (design/RimMandrake/rimflow_v3_trial_night_2026-10-28.md). selftest_dispatcher.py refuses any role enabled but not named in roles, and any seat with recover_dead true but not named in recover_dead. A flip is one file: set the role's enabled true AND add its name here (likewise a seat's recover_dead and its name). The Dispatcher itself does not read this block.

seat_restart._doc: seat_restart.dry true (with enabled true) runs the restart path under the live --apply timer without consuming, killing or launching: the live journal shows restart_request / restart_hold / restart_kill 'would SIGTERM' (the dry ticket in the enable steps). FOUNDRY_CONTEXT_BUILD_FRESH_PER_TICKET (owner 2026-10-28: "Yes we must solve foundry context right now."): a fresh window per ticket. The seat's close-out writes a restart request (seat_restart.py request); the Dispatcher holds it through a grace, while any helper is alive, while the bridge, driver lock or a game action is the seat's, and on any new input, then SIGTERMs that one pid; the tile relaunches itself (seat_loop.sh -> seat_restart.py intile) with the WT profile's own LAUNCH line (--remote-control, --name) plus a first prompt that runs `seat_restart.py wake`; verified once the doorbell re-arms. Every step journalled; failures alarm. Off until the enable steps in design/RimMandrake/rimflow_v3_golive_wave1.md (Seat restart) are done. Keys per seat override seat_restart.DEFAULTS.

Basis (ROLE_CAPS_REMEASURE_ON_REAL_RUNS, BENCH 2026-10-28): the first real role run, D:\ClaudeWork\rimmandrake\dispatcher\roles\rm-role-operations-1793226998.json (Operations alarm run, opus, 15 turns, 105 s): 285,538 weighted (1,121,450 raw, 93% cache reads). a batch runs judge helpers, so run 500,000 = 1.75x that run; daily 1,250,000 = 2 batches x 1.25. roles._why: verdicts advisory: blocks nothing, logs D:\ClaudeWork\rimmandrake\arbiter\verdicts.jsonl beside the interim GPT reviewer (sim findings 3-4: a binding Arbiter on today's quotas mostly defers work; its false-reject rate is unmeasured, RIMFLOW_ARBITER_MEASURE_FALSE_REJECTS). binding = owner's switch after >= 1 week advisory and a MEASURED false-reject rate on >= 30 verdicts. slot_when pending_work (ARBITER_BUILD_LAUNCH_ON_ANY_PENDING_WORK, arbiter_pending.py): a batch launches when any of its four kinds has work, read from state (the ledger, arbiter\verdicts.jsonl, arbiter_tiers\tiers_history.jsonl), never from a cursor. So a launch consumes nothing: a claim stays pending until verdicts.jsonl holds a final verdict for its item and sha (or the no-AI tiers PASS it), an escape until its check spec is filed. Nothing pending: the slot is a hold, no run. Unreadable stores: the slot launches. The queue is the work after the cutoff stamped at enable (ARBITER_DECIDE_BACKLOG_NEVER_DRAINS, BENCH delegated ruling 2026-10-27): no age limit, oldest first (ARBITER_FIX_CLAIMS_AGE_OUT_UNJUDGED retired claim_window_days, which dropped unjudged claims after 7 days); the pre-enable backlog goes to the Auditor's risk-ranked sampling and audit_prescreen's hard flags, never to this queue. No stamp: the slot holds with alarm role:Arbiter:cutoff. The batches stay at the clock (arbiter.md: batched into its 11:00/17:00 runs). helpers_max 2 (sim finding 5) is read by the instructions and the slot allocator's owner, not by role_launch.py. seat/clone/model are the builder's defaults of 2026-10-27 (model opus per rimflow_v3_roles.html), kept when the owner enabled the role (4d9171a1e5).

account_pick._doc: account_pick.py (owner 2026-10-27 [O]: "Dispatch should be able to recognize that the system should switch to a new account before new work is released (when appropriate)"). Before a role launch, a ring or a recover the Dispatcher applies this rule to ops_watch status.json accounts.<label>.*: KEEP / SWITCH / UNMEASURED, noted on ledger_item when it changes. act recommend [A]: a SWITCH holds the kinds in hold and alarms the target; nothing runs claude-account (one account per machine, closes every window, machine DISARMED). Unmeasured current account: keep and alarm, never guess [O]. Lent accounts are the allocator's lent_rules data (<= 50% of his week, only right after his reset [O 2026-10-27], never under the 10% floor, off-limits dates [O]) judged by slot_allocator.lent_allowance; a lent account is a target only when no owned one is fit [O standing ruling]. Thresholds [A]: switch_when 0.8 = under the RED/AMBER line where the bands already shrink work; target 1.2 / 20% = a target that would not itself be switched away from within the day; lent_min_draw_pct 10 = not worth closing every window for less. rank soonest_reset [A]: use-it-or-lose-it.
